memory_update.text: Pure-play remote proctoring and secure-browser vendors appear mostly private or nonprofit-owned; public-market exposure is more likely through Pearson, Duolingo, identity-verification vendors, background/credential verification platforms, or diversified education/testing companies.

MITK is a small-cap underfollowed hypothesis for the identity-proofing/fraud-detection layer of online exam security; survival requires proof of education, proctoring, credentialing, or public-sector exam customers.

FA is an adjacent underfollowed workforce-credential verification candidate rather than a direct exam-security vendor; survival requires evidence that online education/certification volume drives education, license, or credential verification demand.

The node's chokepoint feature bundle appears to include secure test application/browser, government-ID capture, biometric/face matching, room/environment scan, AI fraud detection, human proctor review, audit/compliance documentation, accessibility, and appeal/review workflows.

node: Assessment integrity, remote proctoring, identity verification, and exam security
summary: Layer 1B expanded the US-listed universe for the assessment-integrity/identity node. The directly investable universe is narrow because many pure-play proctoring and secure-browser vendors appear private or nonprofit-owned, including Respondus, Proctorio, Honorlock, ProctorU/Meazure, Examity, ETS, Prometric, Kryterion, Caveon, and ID.me. The most relevant public names are therefore either reference platforms with direct high-stakes testing operations or underfollowed second-order identity/workforce-verification suppliers. No trading recommendation is implied.
